description.text: Protecting Students on Campus Act of 2025 This bill requires the Department of Education (ED) and institutions of higher education (IHEs) participating in federal student aid programs to distribute information on how to report alleged violations of civil rights under Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964. (Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 prohibits discrimination based on race, color, or national origin in federally funded programs or activities.) Specifically, the bill requires ED's Office for Civil Rights (OCR) to conduct a public awareness campaign regarding the rights of individuals under Title VI. This campaign must be updated annually and distributed to IHEs. The bill requires an IHE to post a link on its website on how to file a Title VI complaint with OCR. Additionally, the IHE must annually post the materials from OCR's public awareness campaign. The information must be posted in high-traffic public places on campus (e.g., student centers) and high-traffic websites (e.g., the website for student services). OCR must give monthly congressional briefings on (1) the number of complaints filed with OCR, (2) how OCR plans to address those complaints and the investigations opened in response to those complaints, and (3) how long those complaints remain open. The bill also requires annual reporting by IHEs on discrimination complaints. Further, the bill directs ED's Office of Inspector General to audit and study discrimination complaints.

description.text: DETECT Nitazenes Act of 2025

impact.summary: The bill adds "nitazenes" to the Homeland Security Act's list alongside fentanyl and xylazine. It directs DHS Science and Technology Directorate to work with the Drug Enforcement Administration to develop detection and identification of nitazenes at very low concentrations.

latestAction.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.

bills.title: DETECT Nitazenes Act of 2025

aiDescription.summary: The bill renames D.C.'s Office of Mayor to Office of Governor and the Council to the Legislative Assembly, treating current holders as governor and representatives. It amends the Home Rule Act to make federal and D.C. laws and rules that mention those offices refer to the new titles.

description.text: District of Columbia Government Title Equality Act This bill amends the District of Columbia (DC) Home Rule Act to change the titles of DC elected officials and offices so that the titles correspond to terms used by state governments. Under the bill, the Office of the Mayor becomes the Office of the Governor, the Council becomes the Legislative Assembly, and the Chairman of the Council becomes the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly.

impact.summary: The bill renames the Mayor of the District of Columbia as Governor and the Council as the Legislative Assembly. It treats current officeholders as the new titles and changes references in U.S. and D.C. laws, affecting federal agencies and District government.

latestAction.text: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.

bills.title: District of Columbia Government Title Equality Act

aiDescription.summary: The Act directs U.S. policy to prioritize defense cooperation, using existing security‑assistance authorities to strengthen resilience, logistics, and interoperability. It defines Eastern Flank partners as Bulgaria, Estonia, Finland, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, Romania, and Slovakia and targets 5% of GDP for defense by 2035.

description.text: Eastern Flank Strategic Partnership Act of 2025

impact.summary: The bill directs U.S. defense cooperation with frontline NATO allies Bulgaria, Estonia, Finland, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, Romania, and Slovakia. It authorizes use of FMF, DoD section 333, excess defense-article transfers, and War Reserve Stocks, engaging State and DoD to improve logistics, resilience, and interoperability.

latestAction.text: Referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, and in addition to the Committee on Armed Services, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.

bills.title: Eastern Flank Strategic Partnership Act of 2025

aiDescription.summary: This House resolution supports recognizing September 29, 2025, as "International Day of Awareness of Food Loss and Waste" and urges attention to food‑waste prevention. description.text: This resolution expresses support for the recognition of International Day of Awareness of Food Loss and Waste.

aiDescription.summary: This House resolution designates September 29, 2025, as "National Coffee Day" and supports strengthening coffee supply chains, agricultural research, climate resilience, and coffee health research. It recognizes growers, importers, roasters, retailers, baristas, researchers, U.S. economic impacts and exports, domestic producers in Hawai'i and Puerto Rico, and global smallholder farmers.

description.text: This resolution supports the designation of National Coffee Day. Among other things, the resolution also supports efforts to strengthen domestic and global coffee supply chains and encourages continued scientific research into the health effects of drinking coffee.

aiDescription.summary: The bill creates a National Gun Violence Research Program, authorizes competitive grants and HHS funding for gun-violence research, and lifts restrictions on ATF firearms-trace data. It applies to federal agencies, grant recipients, and institutions studying the causes, consequences, and prevention of gun violence, suicide, unintentional firearm injury, and trafficking.

description.text: National Gun Violence Research Act of 2025 This bill promotes gun violence research, including by removing limitations on the use of firearms tracing data by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives; permitting funds made available to the Department of Health and Human Services to be used for gun violence research; establishing the National Gun Violence Research Program to promote gun violence research; and authorizing competitive grants to support research into the nature, causes, consequences, and prevention of gun violence.

impact.summary: The bill removes limits on ATF firearms tracing data and creates a National Gun Violence Research Program at the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy. It allows HHS funds to support gun-violence research and authorizes competitive grants to universities and public health researchers.

latestAction.text: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.

aiDescription.summary: The bill revises Title I’s definition of “State” to treat American Samoa and the Northern Mariana Islands as separate States for JAG formula grants. Each would receive its own Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant allocation rather than share a single combined allocation.

description.text: Northern Mariana Islands and American Samoa Criminal Justice Support Act This bill increases the amount of state formula grant funds allocated to American Samoa and the Northern Mariana Islands under the Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant (JAG) program. Currently, American Samoa and the Northern Mariana Islands are considered to be one state, and they split one JAG allocation with 67% going to American Samoa and 33% going to the Northern Mariana Islands. This bill considers American Samoa and the Northern Mariana Islands to be separate states, which entitles each of them to a full JAG allocation.

impact.summary: The bill treats American Samoa and the Northern Mariana Islands as separate "States" for the Justice Assistance Grant (JAG) formula. That change requires the Department of Justice to give each territory its own full JAG allocation, increasing funds for local police, prosecutors, and courts.

latestAction.text: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.

bills.title: Northern Mariana Islands and American Samoa Criminal Justice Support Act

aiDescription.summary: The Justice for Exonerees Act raises the cap in 28 U.S.C. 2513(e) from $50,000 to $70,000 and requires annual CPI-based inflation adjustments to awards under that subsection. It covers persons unjustly convicted and imprisoned who obtain damages under that federal statute against the United States.

description.text: Justice for Exonerees Act This bill increases the maximum amount of damages that an individual who was unjustly convicted and incarcerated may be awarded and requires that this amount be adjusted annually for inflation.

impact.summary: The bill raises the maximum federal damage award for an unjust conviction and imprisonment under 28 U.S.C. §2513 from $50,000 to $70,000 and requires annual inflation adjustments tied to the Consumer Price Index. It affects exonerees, the Department of Justice, federal courts, and Treasury.

latestAction.text: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.

bills.title: Justice for Exonerees Act
